knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Hot, swollen, discharging and painful findings are referral signs. The groomer describes the finding, notifies the owner and recommends a vet visit, without treating.
The groomer does not diagnose. The specks are described factually and the owner is advised to ask a vet.
The check is done at the start and at the end of each groom, so changes can be seen.

practicalCriteria: Assessor observes the candidate carry out the systematic check on a simulated animal in the set order, at the start and end of the groom
Assessor presents a simulated referral finding and observes the candidate describe it factually, with no diagnosis, and notify the simulated owner
Assessor checks that the candidate's finding record includes the description, location, size, time and owner response
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Start-and-end check sheet for the simulated groom
Finding record with description, location, size and time
Owner notification record with the response
stopWorkCriteria: The candidate names a diagnosis or applies a product to treat a finding
The candidate photographs a finding without written owner consent
